events.body:

C2: The driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach to the pickup was 2138 m and he never came within 200 m, so the 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' condition of NS-1(ii) fails outright. [F1] [NS-1]
C3: NS-1(iii) also fails: with no arrival confirmation at all, there is no record of the driver waiting continuously more than 3 minutes at the pickup point after a tap; the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance, and the driver's own statement confirms he was still on his way. [F2 F4 F8] [NS-1]
C4: Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, NS-2 applies and the full $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded to the rider. [F1 F4 F5] [NS-2 NS-0]
C5: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching, i.e. within 3 minutes (≤ 3:00), and the rider-branch free-cancellation window of NS-4 independently supports that no fee is chargeable; alternatively the fee is refunded in full. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
C6: No traffic incident was recorded near the route, weather was fair, and only an ordinary band-3 speed reading (20–29 km/h) appears, so nothing excuses the driver's absence 2 km from the pickup or supports any charge on the rider. [F9 F10 F11] [NS-1 NS-2]

C8: The dispute was filed by the rider in this case immediately after the 12:55:40 cancellation, within the 30-day window, so the refund should be issued as a Ryde voucher of $6.61 per NS-7. [F2 F5] [NS-7]

NS-1(iii) also fails: with no arrival confirmation at all, there is no record of the driver waiting continuously more than 3 minutes at the pickup point after a tap; the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance, and the driver's own statement confirms he was still on his way.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, NS-2 applies and the full $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded to the rider.

The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching, i.e. within 3 minutes (≤ 3:00), and the rider-branch free-cancellation window of NS-4 independently supports that no fee is chargeable; alternatively the fee is refunded in full.

events.body:
D1: Ryde's cancellation fee for a rider cancellation only becomes chargeable after 3 minutes from matching; here the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance at 12:54:00, i.e. 12:55:40, which is within the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 fee was not chargeable to the rider. [F2 F5] [NS-0 NS-4]
D2: The rider's complaint is factually correct on the charge: the record shows a $6.61 cancellation fee on a rider cancellation made 1 min 40 s after acceptance, with no surge multiplier (1.0×) that could otherwise enlarge or justify any charge. [F2 F5 F6] [NS-4 NS-0]
D3: No no-show branch applies on this record: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and no arrival confirmation exists, so the driver neither tapped "I'm Here" nor was auto-detected as arrived, and the NS-1 route to validating a passenger no-show is not open — the fee is an unauthorised rider-side charge. [F3 F4] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
D4: The GPS record confirms the rider's account that the driver was far from the pickup: the driver's closest approach was 2138 m at 12:55:40 and he never came within 200 m, a system record that outweighs the driver's own statement that he "was on his way". [F1 F8] [NS-0 NS-4]
D5: Nothing in the record supports a no-show defence: there is no in-app chat at all and no traffic incident near the route, and the only mild congestion (EU TONG SEN STREET, band 3 = 20–29 km/h) does not explain the driver being over 2 km away at the moment the rider cancelled. [F7 F9 F10 F1] [NS-0 NS-1]
D6: The rider's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days (2 of 2 upheld), which is relevant context on the pattern but is not evidence of the facts of this trip and cannot by itself decide it. [F12] [NS-0]
D7: The driver's profile is clean and long-standing — 1839 days on the platform, 4.76 rating, 649 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld — so no dishonest no-show pattern emerges; I ask the judge to rest the ruling on the timeline and GPS records alone. [F13 F2 F3 F4] [NS-0]

Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so NS-0 routes the case to the rider branch, NS-4 [RD? no — NS-0]. Under NS-4 a rider cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching is chargeable, but here acceptance was 12:54:00 and cancellation 12:55:40, i.e. 1 min 40 s, well inside the 3-minute free window [F2], so the $6.61 shown in the fare record [F5] was not chargeable. This alone requires full refund of the fee.

Independently, even on the driver/no-show branch the fee cannot stand: NS-1 requires (i) an "I'm Here" tap or auto-arrival, (ii) GPS at the pickup within range at that moment, and (iii) a continuous wait over 3 minutes; the record shows driver_arrived_at is null [F3] and driver_pressed_here_at is null [F4], and the driver's closest approach was 2138 m, never within 200 m [F1]. So NS-1 fails on all three limbs and NS-2 requires full refund. The driver's post-trip statement that he "was on his way" [F8] is contradicted by the GPS record [F1] and is a statement, not a system record, so it does not displace the trace.

The traffic and weather facts do not assist the driver: no incident near the route [F10], fair weather [F11], and only an ordinary band-3 (20–29 km/h) reading on EU TONG SEN STREET [F9], which explains neither the deviation nor the 2 km distance [F1]; it does not meet the incident/band corroboration requirements.

The arbitration form is a voucher, not cash: the $6.61 is to be returned as a Ryde voucher of $6.61 [F5] under NS-7. No flag_account is added: NS-2's flag applies only where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while outside the pickup radius, which he never did [F4], and the profiles [F12][F13] cannot decide the case or trigger an account action on their own.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement [F8] and the (empty) chat record [F7]; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern = none.

Evidence: the record settles every element needed — the timeline [F2][F3], the GPS distance [F1] and the fare [F5] — so evidence_status = sufficient.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand if NS-1 is met, and it is not: the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and the platform recorded no automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null), and no arrival was ever recorded (driver_arrived_at is null).

The driver was never at the pickup point: his closest approach to the pickup was 2138 m and he never came within 200 m, so the 'at the pick-up location according to GPS data' condition of NS-1(ii) fails outright.

NS-1(iii) also fails: with no arrival confirmation at all, there is no record of the driver waiting continuously more than 3 minutes at the pickup point after a tap; the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance, and the driver's own statement confirms he was still on his way.
Because NS-1 (i), (ii) and (iii) all fail, NS-2 applies and the full $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded to the rider.

The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching, i.e. within 3 minutes (≤ 3:00), and the rider-branch free-cancellation window of NS-4 independently supports that no fee is chargeable; alternatively the fee is refunded in full.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route, weather was fair, and only an ordinary band-3 speed reading (20–29 km/h) appears, so nothing excuses the driver's absence 2 km from the pickup or supports any charge on the rider.

The rider's 90-day no-show disputes were both upheld and the driver has 649 trips in 90 days, so the file shows a rider who is refunded when she is right; the driver's record here shows no arrival data to support the charge. (Profile only supports the outcome, not the finding.)
The dispute was filed by the rider in this case immediately after the 12:55:40 cancellation, within the 30-day window, so the refund should be issued as a Ryde voucher of $6.61 per NS-7.

weaknesses: The rider herself cancelled (F2), so if the judge treats the case as rider-branch NS-4 rather than driver-branch NS-1/NS-2, the outcome still turns on the same 3-minute computation; NS-4's caption says a fee stands after 3 minutes and the record is 1:40, but a judge inclined to read the record loosely in the driver's favour could find ambiguity in the second-level timestamps (F2).

There is no in-app chat at all (F7), so I cannot show any rider message; conversely the driver's statement 'I was on his way' (F8) is the only human account and is contradicted by the GPS record (F1), which the system says wins — but a judge uneasy with one-sided system evidence may be tempted to weigh the statement.

The driver's profile (F13) shows a long, clean history with 0 upheld disputes, which the driver's advocate will use to argue the fee was routine and not abusive, weakening any implication of abuse under NS-2; I therefore ask only for the fee refund, not for a flag_account action against the driver.

claims.assertion: Ryde's cancellation fee for a rider cancellation only becomes chargeable after 3 minutes from matching; here the rider cancelled 1 min 40 s after acceptance at 12:54:00, i.e. 12:55:40, which is within the 3-minute window, so the $6.61 fee was not chargeable to the rider.

The rider's complaint is factually correct on the charge: the record shows a $6.61 cancellation fee on a rider cancellation made 1 min 40 s after acceptance, with no surge multiplier (1.0×) that could otherwise enlarge or justify any charge.

No no-show branch applies on this record: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null) and no arrival confirmation exists, so the driver neither tapped "I'm Here" nor was auto-detected as arrived, and the NS-1 route to validating a passenger no-show is not open — the fee is an unauthorised rider-side charge.

The GPS record confirms the rider's account that the driver was far from the pickup: the driver's closest approach was 2138 m at 12:55:40 and he never came within 200 m, a system record that outweighs the driver's own statement that he "was on his way".

Nothing in the record supports a no-show defence: there is no in-app chat at all and no traffic incident near the route, and the only mild congestion (EU TONG SEN STREET, band 3 = 20–29 km/h) does not explain the driver being over 2 km away at the moment the rider cancelled.

The rider's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in the last 90 days (2 of 2 upheld), which is relevant context on the pattern but is not evidence of the facts of this trip and cannot by itself decide it.

The driver's profile is clean and long-standing — 1839 days on the platform, 4.76 rating, 649 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes upheld — so no dishonest no-show pattern emerges; I ask the judge to rest the ruling on the timeline and GPS records alone.

weaknesses: The rider did not wait out the free-cancellation window cleanly enough to be blameless on timing: F2 shows cancellation at 1 min 40 s, which is the very fact that both helps the rider and shows the rider pulled the plug quickly rather than letting the driver arrive — the other side will argue the rider had no basis to assess the driver's position at 12:55:40.

The driver's written statement (F8) asserts a legitimate reason for not being at the pickup, and although F1 (2138 m closest approach, never within 200 m) contradicts it, the driver will argue there is no record of what traffic or pickup-point approach constraints he faced — F9 (band 3, 20–29 km/h on EU TONG SEN STREET) is the one fact he can cite as some congestion on the corridor.

F12 (rider: 2 no-show disputes in 90 d, 2 upheld) will be used by the rider's side against any inference that this complaint is opportunistic, and it also shows a history of routing/no-show friction that a judge may weigh as neutral context.

There is no chat record at all (F7), so neither side can show an agreement, an ETA message or a mutual arrangement; the case rests entirely on the timeline and GPS facts, and any gap in those records would push the matter to a human under the incompleteness rule.

points.response: Adopted: the opponent's own brief concedes that a rider-side cancellation 1 min 40 s after acceptance is within the NS-4 free-cancellation window, which is exactly the ground on which the $6.61 must be returned.
Adopted: the fare record shows the $6.61 as a cancellation fee and no surge (1.0×), so nothing enlarges or independently justifies what was charged to my client.
Adopted: no arrival was ever recorded (driver_arrived_at is null) and there was no arrival confirmation at all, so NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fail and NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full.

Adopted: the GPS record (2138 m closest approach, never within 200 m) is a system record and, under the system-records-win rule, outweighs the driver's post-trip statement in F8 that he was on his way.

Adopted: there is no chat at all and no traffic incident near the route; the band-3 reading (20–29 km/h) on EU TONG SEN STREET is nowhere near the band-1/band-2 threshold that could ever excuse a reroute, and it does not explain a driver 2 km from the pickup.
Adopted with the same caveat: F12 is profile context only and is not the basis of the ruling — the ruling rests on the timeline and GPS records, which independently require a full refund.

The driver's record (F13) is clean and I therefore ask for no flag_account against him; it does not, however, supply the arrival tap or the 200 m proximity that NS-1 requires, both of which are absent on this record.
Clarifying my own claim: F12 is cited only as background on the parties' dispute history and supports neither the finding nor any account action; the finding stands on F1–F5 alone.

I do not contest this and neither does my brief: F3 and F4 show driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are both null, so the NS-1 arrival conditions were never satisfied and the $6.61 has no valid basis on a rider-branch cancellation.
Correct and undisputed: F1 puts the driver's closest approach at 2138 m with the car never inside 200 m, so NS-1(ii) fails outright and the fee cannot be sustained as a no-show charge.

Agreed: with no arrival confirmation on record (F4) there is no tap or platform auto-arrival from which any 3-minute continuous wait at the pickup could be measured, and the fee therefore fails NS-1(iii) as well.

I accept this consequence: because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) all fail, the rider branch governs and the $6.61 is refundable in full; my brief already asks for refund_full of $6.61 on the same records (F2, F5).

Agreed, and I put it the same way in D1: F2 records cancellation 1 min 40 s after acceptance, inside the 3-minute free window, so no fee is chargeable regardless of whether one reasons through NS-4 or through NS-2.

Agreed on the traffic evidence — F10 shows no incident near the route and F9 is only an ordinary band-3 reading on EU TONG SEN STREET — and I add that this cuts against my own client, since nothing in F9–F11 explains his being 2138 m away per F1.

Conceded as to the finding: F12 (rider's 2 no-show disputes both upheld) and F13 (driver's 649 trips) are profile facts that may support an outcome but cannot decide this case, and F3/F4 decide it against the driver on their own.

No objection: F2 places the cancellation on 12:55:40 and the rider's dispute is filed in this case, so the $6.61 goes back as a Ryde voucher under the NS-7 form; I ask only that the ruling rest on F2/F3/F4/F1 rather than on any profile history.

I note my own D4 remains on the record but is now immaterial to the result: F1 (2138 m, never within 200 m) contradicts the driver's statement in F8, and since F3/F4 already defeat the fee, the judge need not choose between them.
